summary:
GLP-1 radar, 28 Sep 2026. EASD 2026 opens today in Milan (Sep 28 to Oct 2), so a wave of GLP-1 abstracts should reach the news over the next 3–7 days. Two EASD items are already getting picked up. The first is an analysis of 313,145 adults in UK Biobank and the Copenhagen study: people with overweight who are not eligible for GLP-1s today but have high remnant cholesterol or inflammation had heart-disease risk similar to people who are eligible. The second is an ATTAIN post-hoc analysis: the orforglipron pill led to similar weight loss (up to about 14%) before, during and after menopause. Both are at the emerging stage and few creators have covered them yet.

The CagriSema story is confusing people. Headlines say it "outperforms Zepbound", but that result comes from a type 2 diabetes trial against a low tirzepatide dose. In REDEFINE 4, the head-to-head obesity trial, CagriSema came in 2.5 points behind tirzepatide 15 mg and missed its non-inferiority goal. We can explain that clearly.

Hair loss is the fastest-rising question from patients. The Guardian and Times of India covered it on Sep 27–28, alongside a Clinical Dermatology review and the BMJ and NYU studies. Several other topics are growing in the news but have little evidence-based YouTube coverage: GLP-1s and cannabis (stomach effects), period changes on semaglutide (FAERS signal), GLP-1s vs CPAP for sleep apnea (JAMA Otolaryngology review), and flu-like symptoms after stopping.

The "stopping raises heart risk" story is resurfacing: it is a March 2026 BMJ Medicine study now spreading through Scripps syndication. It is only safe if framed as "plan any change with your prescriber". Vision-loss (NAION) lawsuits and "microdosing" are rated caution and reject. Covering them would mean fear-bait or content that breaks our guardrails.

Two topics carry over from earlier snapshots. The SELECT mediation analysis is holding at a momentum of about 72, and the tirzepatide brown-fat mouse study is now reaching mainstream outlets. For the brown-fat story, the only safe angle is "mice only".

candidates.topic: Could GLP-1s help millions more people protect their heart? EASD 2026 study of 313,145 adults with overweight (UK Biobank + Copenhagen)
candidates.angle: 'Your BMI isn't the whole story.' In adults with a BMI of 25–27 who are not currently eligible, the roughly half with high remnant cholesterol or low-grade inflammation had heart-disease risk similar to people who qualify for GLP-1s today. Explain which blood markers to ask your doctor about. Be clear this is an observational risk study: it did not test the drugs, and trials are still needed.
candidates.why_now: Presented at EASD 2026, which opens today. Medical Xpress covered it on Sep 27 and Google News picked it up. Almost no creator videos yet. It fits the 'who may benefit, questions for your doctor' pillar.

evidence.signal: 313,145 participants; 23,134 developed coronary heart disease over 10–18 years; 44–48% of those with BMI 25–26.9 had elevated remnant cholesterol or inflammation, with heart risk similar to eligible groups; researchers say trials are needed

candidates.topic: The orforglipron pill (Foundayo) led to similar weight loss before, during and after menopause (ATTAIN-1/2 post-hoc, EASD 2026)
candidates.angle: 'Does menopause stop GLP-1s from working?' In this analysis, women lost similar amounts of weight in all three stages: up to about 14%, with up to 83% losing at least 5% (vs 30% on placebo). Also cover what this means for the 'menopause belly' question. Flag that it is a post-hoc analysis with 142–225 women per group.
candidates.why_now: Medscape and Medical Xpress covered it on Sep 26 and it is being presented at EASD this week. Menopause plus GLP-1 is a high-demand topic for our audience of women aged 40–65, and oral GLP-1 prescriptions are rising (Fierce Pharma tracker).

evidence.signal: Up to 14% weight loss across pre-, peri- and postmenopause; up to 83% lost at least 5% vs 30% on placebo; waist down up to 12.5 cm; 72 weeks; post-hoc analysis
Orforglipron Aids Weight Loss Across Menopausal Stages

candidates.topic: GLP-1 hair loss: how common it really is, why it happens, and what helps (BMJ 2026, NYU/JID study, Clinical Dermatology review)
candidates.angle: Calm, practical explainer. Hair loss is linked to GLP-1 use, but the absolute risk is low. Much of the shedding is likely telogen effluvium from rapid weight loss and low protein intake, and it usually recovers. Cover protein, iron and nutrient checks with your doctor. Correct the 'Ozempic makes you bald' myth.
candidates.why_now: The Guardian (Sep 27) and Times of India (Sep 28) both ran hair-loss explainers, a Clinical Dermatology review appeared Sep 21, and NYU findings were published Sep 16. People are searching this question heavily.

evidence.signal: GLP-1 users with type 2 diabetes developed alopecia more often than users of other diabetes drugs; absolute risk low
Hair and Scalp Effects of GLP-1 Receptor Agonists in Practice (Sep 21)
NYU Langone study: GLP-1 use may speed up hair loss in predisposed men

candidates.topic: Did CagriSema really beat Zepbound? Two trials, two different answers (REIMAGINE in type 2 diabetes vs REDEFINE 4 in obesity)
candidates.angle: Headline decoder. The 'beats Zepbound' result compared CagriSema with a low 5 mg tirzepatide dose in people with type 2 diabetes (12.4% vs 9.1%). In the head-to-head obesity trial, CagriSema reached 23.0% vs 25.5% for tirzepatide 15 mg and missed non-inferiority. Explain how amylin works and what's next (FDA decision expected Q4 2026).
candidates.why_now: AOL, Yahoo and NewsNation all ran 'outperforms Zepbound' on Sep 27, while trade press says it 'fails to match'. The confusion is our opening, and there is an FDA decision in Q4.

evidence.signal: CagriSema 12.4% vs tirzepatide 5 mg 9.1% at 60 weeks in type 2 diabetes; FDA decision expected Q4 2026
Novo's next-gen obesity shot fails to match Lilly drug in head-to-head study
REDEFINE 4: 23.0% vs 25.5% at 84 weeks, 809 adults; non-inferiority not met

candidates.topic: GLP-1s and sleep apnea: fewer breathing pauses, but CPAP still works better (JAMA Otolaryngology review)
candidates.angle: 'Can Zepbound replace your CPAP?' GLP-1s cut apnea events by about 6–22 per hour (tirzepatide strongest), compared with about 31 per hour for CPAP. Present them as a teammate, not a replacement. Tirzepatide is FDA-approved for moderate-to-severe OSA in adults with obesity. Never tell anyone to stop CPAP.
keywords: can I stop CPAP on Mounjaro
candidates.why_now: Nexstar syndication (KTLA, KRQE, AOL, MSN) ran it Sep 26–28, and Bioengineer published 'Weight-loss drugs are redrawing sleep medicine'. It fits the 'benefits beyond weight' pillar.

evidence.signal: GLP-1s reduced events by 6–22 per hour vs CPAP ~31 per hour; JAMA Otolaryngology–Head & Neck Surgery review

candidates.topic: Weight loss explains only about 20% of semaglutide's heart benefit (SELECT mediation analysis, European Heart Journal)
candidates.angle: 'It's not just the scale.' If weight loss accounts for only about a fifth of the lower heart-event risk in SELECT, what explains the rest? Cover inflammation, blood pressure and direct effects on blood vessels. State the population precisely: adults with heart disease and overweight or obesity, without diabetes.
candidates.why_now: Seen in 5 snapshots at a steady 70–76. News-Medical (Sep 28) and Medical Dialogues are still covering it, and it pairs with the EASD eligibility study.

evidence.signal: Semaglutide and cardiovascular risk reduction: a mediation analysis of the SELECT trial
'Researchers still cannot fully explain why' (Sep 28)

candidates.topic: GLP-1s and cannabis: why the combination may raise the risk of stomach problems
candidates.angle: How it works, without judgment: both GLP-1s and cannabis can slow stomach emptying, and cannabinoid hyperemesis can look like GLP-1 nausea. Explain what to tell your prescriber and which warning signs need care. The evidence is mostly case reports and expert opinion, so hedge accordingly.
candidates.why_now: FOX LiveNOW (Sep 27), AOL (Sep 28) and the FOX local stations are all covering it, and it is a common search question. Evidence-based videos are scarce.

evidence.signal: Using cannabis with GLP-1 drugs may heighten stomach issue risk
Intractable vomiting with GLP-1 RA and cannabis use

candidates.topic: Period changes on semaglutide: heavy bleeding and skipped ovulation flagged in FDA adverse-event reports
candidates.angle: Straight facts for women of reproductive age. This is a reporting signal from FAERS, not proof that the drug causes it, and weight loss itself shifts hormones. Tirzepatide showed a narrower signal and liraglutide none. Add a note on fertility and contraception to discuss with a clinician. Do not claim causation.
candidates.why_now: Yahoo Health ran it Sep 26 and Medscape covered the FAERS analysis. This is a question women are clearly asking, and almost no one covers it carefully.

evidence.signal: Menstrual clots and heavy bleeding linked to popular weight-loss drugs (FAERS disproportionality analysis)
Semaglutide was linked to changes in women's periods, including heavy bleeding and missed ovulation

candidates.topic: Why GLP-1 benefits can fade if you stop: the 'metabolic whiplash' study (333,000 veterans, BMJ Medicine)
candidates.angle: This is a staying-on-track topic, not a scare. When people stopped, weight, blood pressure, cholesterol and inflammation all tended to rebound. The study found up to 22% higher risk of heart attack, stroke or death after 2 years off treatment, in veterans with type 2 diabetes (observational). The takeaway: any change should be a plan made with your prescriber, plus the habits that help keep results.
keywords: what happens when you stop Wegovy
candidates.why_now: The March 2026 BMJ Medicine study is resurfacing through Scripps syndication (Sep 27), alongside 'flu-like symptoms when stopping' pieces in the Mirror and Glasgow Live.

evidence.signal: Stopping GLP-1 drugs can quickly erase cardiovascular benefits
Up to 22% higher risk after 2 years off; 333,000+ veterans with type 2 diabetes

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide switched on calorie-burning brown fat, but so far only in obese mice
candidates.angle: 'Mounjaro burns fat while you rest?' Not proven in humans. Explain what brown fat is and why mouse results often don't carry over to people. The clinically proven effects are appetite and blood sugar.
candidates.why_now: ScienceDaily, Men's Journal, Yahoo Health and Health and Me all ran it Sep 26–27. Momentum rose from 58 to 76 across snapshots, and the overhyped headlines need correcting.

evidence.signal: Zepbound and Mounjaro may turn on the body's calorie-burning brown fat

candidates.topic: Semaglutide and thigh muscle: MRI data from STEP UP on muscle volume, fat infiltration and physical function
candidates.angle: 'Will I lose muscle on Ozempic?' Explain what happened to thigh muscle volume and to fat inside the muscle, and link it to strength training and protein. Pair it with the Clin Nutr paper on creatine as an early, unproven idea, not a recommendation.
candidates.why_now: The STEP UP secondary analysis was published Sep 20 and the creatine commentary Sep 21. Muscle-loss stories keep running (Northwestern RNA therapy in mice), and this topic is a core pillar.

evidence.signal: Effect of semaglutide on thigh muscle volume, fat infiltration and physical function: STEP UP secondary analysis
Creatine for GLP-1-associated muscle loss

candidates.topic: McDonald's and fast-food chains are building menus for GLP-1 users: how to order smart when your appetite is small
candidates.angle: Practical 'life on GLP-1'. Why smaller portions, high protein and fiber matter on GLP-1s. Show how to build a protein-first, lower-fat meal when eating out (fatty meals can worsen nausea). No brand endorsements.
candidates.why_now: CBS (Sep 25), KTLA and WKRN (Sep 28), and Yahoo Finance are all on it. The food-culture angle has viral reach, and the Business Insider dietitian tips back it up.

evidence.signal: How GLP-1 weight-loss drugs are changing fast-food menus

candidates.topic: Why GLP-1s work less for some people: 'non-responders' and what predicted bigger weight loss in SELECT
candidates.angle: 'It's not your fault.' Up to about 15% of people see a limited effect. Cover what the SELECT predictors analysis found about who lost the most weight, and what to discuss with your doctor if progress stalls (no dose advice).
keywords: why am I not losing weight on Mounjaro
candidates.why_now: The Diabetes Care SELECT predictors paper appeared Sep 24, DongA Science reported 'limited effect in up to 15%' on Sep 27, and nj.com's 'Dear Doctor' column shows patients asking.

evidence.signal: Predictors of peak body weight loss with semaglutide in the SELECT trial
GLP-1 drugs show limited effect in up to 15% of patients

candidates.topic: Myth check: GLP-1s and pancreatitis or pancreatic cancer (global propensity-matched cohort in type 2 diabetes)
candidates.angle: Reassuring but honest. This large matched cohort found no increased risk of pancreatitis or pancreatic cancer in people with type 2 diabetes. Explain what 'observational' means, why the label warnings still exist, and which symptoms need urgent care.
candidates.why_now: The J Pers Med study was published Sep 16, and safety headlines (lawsuits) are raising anxiety. A myth-correction post fits our tone.

evidence.signal: GLP-1 RAs not associated with increased acute pancreatitis or pancreatic cancer risk in type 2 diabetes

candidates.topic: GLP-1s and the brain: slower dementia progression in type 2 diabetes with mild cognitive impairment (target-trial emulation), and lessons from the negative EVOKE trials
candidates.angle: 'Can Ozempic protect your brain?' Balance the hopeful real-world signal against the EVOKE result, where semaglutide did not slow early Alzheimer's. Explain why observational and randomized results can disagree.
candidates.why_now: Two fresh papers, Sep 20 and Sep 24. Brain health is a strong pillar for our audience, and the story needs a nuanced take.

evidence.signal: Dementia progression with GLP-1 RAs in MCI and type 2 diabetes: target-trial emulation
EVOKE(+) trials of semaglutide for early Alzheimer's: lessons

candidates.topic: Fake GLP-1 scams: the Better Business Bureau warning and how to recognize legitimate care
candidates.angle: Consumer protection only. Cover the red flags (no prescription, 'research use only', huge discounts, social media DMs) and why a licensed prescriber and pharmacy matter. Never name or link any source for buying.
candidates.why_now: The BBB warning ran Sep 25 (ABC7). The Philippines FDA issued an advisory on unregistered 'retatrutide 30 mg' (Sep 26), and there are FDA compounding warning letters.

evidence.signal: GLP-1 scammers selling fake weight-loss drugs, BBB warns

candidates.angle: Only a later, sober explainer would be acceptable, focused on what the evidence shows (a rare, debated association) and 'report sudden vision changes'. Current coverage is driven by lawsuits and fear.
candidates.why_now: A flurry of lawsuit stories (NewsNation, MassLive, KOAT), where an expert says causation will be 'hard to prove'.

evidence.signal: Expert says GLP-1 vision loss claims will be 'hard to prove'

candidates.angle: Do not cover. Microdosing and self-titration protocols are explicitly off-limits for the brand.
candidates.why_now: A Yahoo Creators piece on Sep 27 is spreading it.

evidence.signal: Is microdosing Ozempic safe?
